# versioned tarball below) and read VERSION.txt inside it.

notes: v62 fixes the compiler crash Lars hit in every incremental Lazarus IDE build since v59: when a unit that other units had already been compiled against turned out to need recompiling (its implementation uses a unit whose checksum changed -- a uses-cycle through an implementation section defers that check), the compiler "reloaded" those source-compiled units, which only re-resolves deref tables; a source unit has none for its implementation side, so it kept pointers into the freed symtable and crashed in tderef.build under writeppu (EAccessViolation, exit 217). Fix ade0c47fc4 (compiler/fmodule.pas +32): such a dependent is recompiled from source instead, exactly as the checksum-mismatch path already did; units loaded from a .ppu keep the reload. The same defect is in upstream FPC main. Compiler-binary-only refresh on the v61 tarball tree: no PPU format, RTL or package change, so UNITS ARE STILL THE v52 SET and auto-update.bat can take the ~3.5 MB bin tarball alone; every bin/ member but ppcx64.exe is byte-identical to v61/v60/v59. ppcx64.exe is 5055488 bytes here, which is NOT the 5054976 the v59, v60 and v61 exes all shared -- the size moved for the first time in four releases, which is exactly why the rule is to verify by md5 and never by size. date: is the compiler's own -iD stamp. VERIFIED with the x86_64-linux compiler from the same source on the two-step Lazarus rig (v59 and v61 die, this source links the IDE) and dist/ppu-reload-check.sh (v59/v61 FAIL, v62 PASS); this exe passed dist/win64-runtime-proof.sh under wine64. HONEST LIMIT: wine is NOT Windows; v59 ran on native Windows (2026-09-17), v60/v61/v62 have not. Full record: dist/RELEASE-v62.txt and dist/win64/staging-v62/VERSION.txt.
